name: Shemaiah
overview: Shemaiah was a male biblical figure identified as a descendant of Adonikam. He is noted for accompanying Ezra during the return to Jerusalem, as recorded in Ezra 8:13. There is no additional tribal or familial information provided beyond this lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Shemaiah means 'YHWH hears,' reflecting a theologically significant Hebrew proper name. This name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaning that underscores God's attentiveness to His people, as noted in Ezra 8:13.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Shemaiah as a descendant of Adonikam, establishing a direct familial link. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shemaiah's significance lies in his role as one of the individuals who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra, marking him as part of the faithful remnant restoring Israel after the exile. His descent from Adonikam connects him to a known family line involved in this important restoration effort. His presence in Ezra 8:13 situates him within the historical narrative of God's providential preservation and the reestablishment of the community under God's covenant.
